responses.explanation: While it is true that maize is bought on the open market, the evidence from ORV-0031 | Page 1 | Paragraph 5 indicates that maize is exposed to the spot market and that feed compounders can only change rations temporarily. This highlights the structural vulnerability of maize supply, contradicting the assertion that alternative suppliers can fully mitigate the impact.

The claim that exposure from maize imports is mitigated by substitute suppliers overlooks the fact that maize is subject to spot market volatility, as stated in ORV-0031 | Page 1 | Paragraph 5. Additionally, the cost of switching rations is already affecting margins, indicating that any mitigation is limited and temporary.
